item.title: SMC Het
item.description:
The ICGC-TCGA DREAM Somatic Mutation Calling Tumor Heterogeneity Challenge (SMC-Het) focused on subclonal reconstruction: determining which cancer-cell populations are present in a tumor and which mutations belong to each population.

Participants were asked to estimate tumor purity and the number and prevalence of subclones, assign mutations to those subclones, and infer their evolutionary relationships. The challenge aimed to compare methods and identify conditions that affect their performance. See the SMC-Het project on Synapse for challenge materials.

item.title: DREAM-SMC
item.description:
The ICGC-TCGA DREAM Somatic Mutation Calling Challenge evaluated methods for identifying cancer-associated mutations from whole-genome sequencing data. Participants analyzed matched tumor and normal samples and submitted calls for single-nucleotide variants and larger genomic rearrangements.

The challenge brought together the International Cancer Genome Consortium, The Cancer Genome Atlas, Sage Bionetworks, and IBM-DREAM to compare algorithms against validation data. The challenge is closed; see the DREAM-SMC project on Synapse for its materials.

item.title: DREAM-SMC-RNA
item.description:
The ICGC-TCGA DREAM Somatic Mutation Calling RNA Challenge (SMC-RNA) compared computational methods for analyzing cancer RNA-sequencing data. Participants developed methods to detect gene fusions and quantify transcript isoforms, both of which can reveal changes in tumor biology.

The challenge was organized with the International Cancer Genome Consortium, The Cancer Genome Atlas, Sage Bionetworks, and IBM-DREAM. It is now closed. Visit the SMC-RNA project on Synapse for its challenge materials.
